claim: Guo, Huang, Gao, Li, Ge, Kuang, Wang (Princeton), 'AQuA: Recursively Self-Improving Quantitative Trading Research Agents', arXiv 2608.12841 (2026-08-13) -- NOT the title the user's GPT summary gave. Two LLM research loops in sealed sandboxes: symbolic factor discovery (crypto, combined validation IC ~0.190) and trainable model development (US equities: per-stock IC +0.0843, held-out 2021-2025 Sharpe +2.50 at 22 bp two-leg cost, ~+2.0 under stricter walk-forward; train 2010-2019, 2020 embargo).
impact_on_spec: Evidence that a closed research loop with sealed test windows can reach IC ~0.08 on US equities, but as a design pattern only: universe, data source, candidate counts and multiple-testing controls are undisclosed and the expressions are withheld.
limitations: 'The deployed expressions are withheld throughout'; no code; universe/bar frequency not disclosed; the 0.0843 IC is the trainable-model system, not discovered factors; selection-bias control rests on governance ('weaker than structural guarantees').

claim: Tian, Xiang, Xu, 'Insider trading and anomalies', Journal of Empirical Finance 84 (Dec 2025) 101666: the fraction of anomaly long-leg (short-leg) stocks bought (sold) by insiders forecasts the anomaly's future long-short return in- and out-of-sample (composite of 11 anomalies); aggregation at the portfolio level washes out firm-specific noise.
impact_on_spec: This is anomaly-level TIMING via aggregated insider trades, not a stock-level 'insider composite factor'. The stock-level recipe the user's GPT summary described belongs to the older opportunistic-vs-routine insider literature (Cohen, Malloy, Pomorski 2012) and must be carded separately before use.
limitations: Abstract-level verification only (paywalled); exact horizon, data vendor and magnitudes not extracted.

claim: Du, Walter, Ulrich, 'Cross-Market Alpha: Testing Short-Term Trading Factors in the U.S. Market via Double-Selection LASSO', arXiv 2601.06499 (v1 2026-01-10, v2 2026-05-21): the 191 signals ARE the GTJA Alpha 191 library ('we source the 191 signals from the GTJA Alpha 191 library'), built on S&P 500 constituents 2002-2022 (OptionMetrics IvyDB, 4,917,327 obs), monthly rebalancing, 168 usable after removing discontinuous variables, 17 survive double-selection LASSO against 151 fundamental controls with t > 2: ids 046, 084, 073, 123, 049, 071, 184, 155, 054, 181, 161, 190, 039, 015, 063, 001, 086 (Table 3; DS lambda 25-79 bp/month).
impact_on_spec: Directly prioritizes the remaining alpha191 port: implement these 17 ids first (our current port has 20 of 191, chosen before this evidence) and screen them with scripts/screen_factors.py; the paper's universe (S&P 500, monthly) differs from ours (PIT top-500 ADV, weekly).
limitations: Monthly horizon and 2002-2022 sample; no IC reported, only DS-LASSO premia and t-stats; survival in a 2024-2026 window untested.

claim: SEC 'Insider Transactions Data Sets': flattened as-filed XML data from Forms 3/4/5, January 2006 through the current period, published quarterly (documents filed after 5:30pm ET on the quarter's last business day roll to the next posting); tables include SUBMISSION, REPORTINGOWNER, NONDERIV_TRANS with FILING_DATE, DOCUMENT_TYPE, ISSUERTRADINGSYMBOL, RPTOWNER_RELATIONSHIP, TRANS_DATE, TRANS_CODE, TRANS_SHARES, TRANS_PRICEPERSHARE, TRANS_ACQUIRED_DISP_CD.
impact_on_spec: Free, official, PIT-capable (FILING_DATE at day granularity; visibility rule = next trading day after filing) source for an insider-trading feature packet: open-market purchases (TRANS_CODE P) and sales (S), officer/director roles, non-routine classification per insider history.
limitations: No acceptance timestamp in the readme grep, so intraday PIT is impossible (day granularity); quarterly publication lag means the live packet needs EDGAR daily Form 4 feeds on top; as-filed data has amendments/duplicates to dedupe.
